immediate_action: Isolate heavily infected plants and prune out the worst leaves with sterilized shears.
Increase greenhouse ventilation immediately to lower leaf-surface humidity.
Avoid overhead irrigation; switch to drip or sub-irrigation.
biological_treatment: Apply Bacillus subtilis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens biofungicide per label rates.
Use potassium bicarbonate or horticultural oil sprays during cooler parts of the day.
Introduce beneficial microbes via compost tea where permitted by local guidance.
chemical_control: Rotate sulfur-based or potassium bicarbonate products early in the infection cycle.
Use labeled systemic fungicides (e.g., myclobutanil / trifloxystrobin group products) only when pressure is high, following PHI and resistance-management rules.
Never tank-mix incompatible oils and sulfur; observe temperature restrictions.
prevention: Maintain plant spacing for airflow and remove lower canopy debris.
Keep relative humidity below ~85% overnight when crop stage allows.
Scout weekly and sanitize tools between plants and rows.
environmental_adjustments: Raise night ventilation setpoint and enable dehumidification cycles.
Reduce dense shading that traps moisture on leaf surfaces.
Balance irrigation to avoid prolonged leaf wetness.
sources: University plant pathology extension guidance (powdery mildew on greenhouse crops)

immediate_action: Remove and destroy infected foliage immediately; do not compost symptomatic material.
Restrict movement between infected and clean zones; sanitize footwear and tools.
Reduce leaf wetness duration with ventilation and irrigation timing changes.
biological_treatment: Deploy copper alternatives / biofungicides labeled for Phytophthora where available as a first soft response.
Support plant vigor with balanced nutrition; avoid excess nitrogen that creates soft tissue.
chemical_control: Apply protectant fungicides (e.g., chlorothalonil / mancozeb-class products where legal) on a tight schedule during weather conducive to blight.
Rotate FRAC groups; include systemic materials labeled for late blight when risk is extreme.
Follow local extension spray alerts and pre-harvest intervals strictly.
prevention: Use certified clean transplants and resistant cultivars when available.
Eliminate volunteer hosts and cull piles near the greenhouse.
Monitor forecasts for cool, wet conditions that favor Phytophthora.
environmental_adjustments: Keep canopy dry; run fans and open vents after irrigation or fog events.
Avoid dense plantings and prolonged RH spikes above 90%.
Improve drainage under benches and eliminate standing water.
sources: USDA / university late blight alerts and IPM manuals

immediate_action: Remove symptomatic leaves and avoid working plants when foliage is wet.
Disinfect pruning tools between plants with 70% alcohol or approved sanitizer.
Quarantine new introductions until scouted clean.
biological_treatment: Apply copper-alternative biologicals and antagonistic bacteria products labeled for bacterial diseases.
Use induced-resistance products where crop labels allow.
chemical_control: Copper bactericides or fixed-copper formulations on a preventive schedule during humid weather.
Avoid overuse that risks phytotoxicity; follow label rates for greenhouse crops.
prevention: Start with disease-free seed/transplants and resistant varieties.
Minimize splash irrigation and worker traffic through wet canopies.
Sanitize benches, trays, and irrigation emitters between cycles.
environmental_adjustments: Lower humidity and increase air exchange after irrigation.
Space plants to speed canopy drying.
Keep night temperatures from encouraging condensation on leaves.

immediate_action: Sanitize dead flowers and senescent leaves that act as infection centers.
Increase airflow and reduce free moisture on flowers and leaves.
Spot-treat early lesions before canopy closure.
biological_treatment: Use biologicals in rotation to reduce chemical reliance.
chemical_control: Rotate labeled greenhouse fungicides by FRAC code.
Target flower and fruit zones carefully for Botrytis-prone crops.
prevention: Avoid prolonged high humidity and dense canopies.
Harvest promptly; remove aborted fruit and petals.
Keep walkways and floors free of plant debris.
environmental_adjustments: Program humidity spikes down with heating + venting pulses.
Irrigate in the morning so foliage dries before night.
Reduce fogging frequency during cool cloudy periods.

immediate_action: Confirm diagnosis with clear photos or lab sampling if symptoms are atypical.
Isolate affected plants and increase scouting frequency to every 24–48 hours.
Record temperature, humidity, and irrigation events around symptom onset.
biological_treatment: Begin with labeled biological protectants suitable for the crop and symptom class.
Support beneficial microbial balance in the root zone and phyllosphere.
chemical_control: Select only products labeled for the crop and suspected pathogen; rotate modes of action.
Consult local extension before broad-spectrum chemical programs.
prevention: Maintain sanitation, clean transplants, and worker hygiene protocols.
Keep climate within crop-optimal bands to reduce abiotic stress that invites disease.
environmental_adjustments: Stabilize VPD, avoid leaf wetness, and ensure adequate air movement.
Review shading and irrigation schedules for stress reduction.
